question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -9 & -3 & -6 \\ 1 & -3 & -3 & -5 \\ -2 & 3 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -9 & -3 & -6 \\ 1 & -3 & -3 & -5 \\ -2 & 3 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 & -3 & -5 \\ -2 & 3 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{3}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{3}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

metadata.domain: x,y,z real; p,q,s nonzero; nonsingular 3-by-3 coefficient matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x+6y &=6 \\ 2x+4y+3z &=8 \\ -x &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 6 & 0 & 6 \\ 2 & 4 & 3 & 8 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 3 & 8 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 4 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=\frac{4}{3} \\ y &=1-(0)\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \\ &=1 \\ x &=2-(2)(1) \\ &\quad -(0)\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(0,1,\frac{4}{3}\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x+3y &=12 \\ -2x+2y+3z &=8 \\ -x+4y-z &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 3 & 0 & 12 \\ -2 & 2 & 3 & 8 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ -2 & 2 & 3 & 8 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=0 \\ y &=0-\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)(0) \\ &=0 \\ x &=-4-(-1)(0) \\ &\quad -(0)(0) \\ &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-4,0,0\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x+6y+6z &=-6 \\ 3x+6y+3z &=-2 \\ -2x-y-2z &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 6 & 6 & -6 \\ 3 & 6 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 3 & 6 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{4}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{4}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{4}{3} \\ y &=-\frac{2}{3}-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{9} \\ x &=-2-(2)\left(\frac{2}{9}\right) \\ &\quad -(2)\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{2}{9},\frac{2}{9},-\frac{4}{3}\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y+4z &=0 \\ 3x+3y+8z &=-5 \\ x-y+z &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 8 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 8 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{5}{2} \\ y &=-1-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{1}{4} \\ x &=0-(1)\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) \\ &\quad -(2)\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{19}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{19}{4},\frac{1}{4},-\frac{5}{2}\right)
$$

\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y+2z &=-8 \\ x-2y-2z &=-2 \\ -2x+2y+3z &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & 2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 3 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 3 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & 3 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x+6y-6z &=3 \\ 3x-6y+3z &=-1 \\ 2x-y+9z &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 6 & -6 & 3 \\ 3 & -6 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 9 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -6 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 9 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 9 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 5 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{2}{3} \\ y &=0-\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{10}{9} \\ x &=-1-(-2)\left(\frac{10}{9}\right) \\ &\quad -(2)\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{23}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{23}{9},\frac{10}{9},-\frac{2}{3}\right)
$$
